notes.1: This question was generally well done and source of good marks.
notes.1i: Many candidates found the correct expressions for x and y in terms of t.
notes.2i: Candidates often used Newton’s Second Law. Unfortunately, sign errors occurred or the weight component was omitted.
notes.2iii: A 3 term energy equation was often seen. Again, as above, sign errors appeared. Answers: (i) Initial acceleration = 70 ms–2
notes.3i: Candidates tried to set up a moment equation. In doing so errors were made.
notes.4iii: ∫ = ∫dt was often seen. On a number of occasions ln(10–0.45v) = t + c was seen 10−0.45v instead of – ln(10–0.45v) = t + c. The value of c was too often incorrectly calculated. Some 0.45 candidates tried to use the rectilinear equations of motion. Answers: (i) a = 10 – 0.45v
notes.5: This question proved to be a good source of marks.
notes.5i: Some candidates found the vertical component of the speed as 50sin40 + 2.5g instead of 50sin40 – 2.5g. The horizontal and vertical components of the speed were usually found. The resultant was then found by using Pythagoras’s theorem.
notes.5iii: On occasions tan θ = v /v was used instead of tan θ = s /s , where θ was the required angle. y x y x Answers: (i) Speed of P = 39.0 ms–1
notes.6: The first part of the question was quite well done. The second part proved to be rather difficult.
notes.6i: a = 1.22/(0.2cos30) was used quite often. Unfortunately at times 0.3x1.22/(0.2cos30) was seen instead of Tcos30 = 0.3x1.22/(0.2cos30). r = 0.2 was used on occasions instead of r = 0.2cos30.
notes.6iii: (a) The correct solution should be. Resolve vertically: Tcos30 = 0.3g, T = 6 Resolve horizontally: 6cos30 = 0.3ω2x(0.2cos30), ω = 10. (Newton’s Second Law)
notes.7: This question proved to be a very difficult one. Many candidates did not score high marks. Answers: θ ≥ 0.224 �PAGE�42

The presentation of the work was good in most cases and usually easy to follow.
Generally g = 10 was used with only a few candidates still using g = 9.8 or 9.81.
